notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Implemented and verified. Unblocked by the maintainer's explicit 2026-08-23 authorization ("OCR licensing is ok, agpl. convert whichever crate to agpl if u need") -- no crate conversion was actually needed since `kovan` is already AGPL-3.0-only (from the earlier kopitiam-pdf relicense).

What shipped:
- `kopitiam-ocr` (0.1.0, AGPL-3.0-only, crates.io) added as a crate-local dependency of `kovan` only, per the same pattern already established for `kopitiam-pdf`. Provenance/licence chain (kopitiam-ocr -> kopitiam-tensor -> kopitiam-core, lean, Android/Termux-clean) documented in `crates/kovan/NOTICE`.
- New `digitiser::table_ocr` module: `RecognizedTable` type + `recognize_table()` (grayscale -> Otsu binarize -> find_text_lines -> per-line LSTM recognition -> cell split), JSON/CSV export with embedded provenance headers. Cell splitting is a whitespace-run heuristic (2+ spaces = column boundary) -- explicitly NOT real table/column detection, documented as a known limitation in the module doc.
- Reuses `dataset::ReviewStatus`/`ReviewInterface` directly (no duplication) -- output always starts UNREVIEWED, only a human GUI action can mark it reviewed.
- PDF reader gained a second crop tool ("Digitise table"), alongside the existing plot-crop tool, via a new `CropKind`/`CropResult` enum pair so the same drag-then-right-click gesture now serves both digitiser tabs.
- New `TableDigitiserState` GUI tab: model-path + operator fields, Run OCR, editable `egui::Grid` review table (any edit resets review to Unreviewed, mirroring the plot digitiser and op-fueb's error-visibility pattern), Mark reviewed, JSON/CSV save, CSV preview.
- Wired into `DigitiseApp`: new `View::TableDigitiser`, top-bar button, PDF-reader crop-result dispatch routes `CropResult::Table` here.

Verified:
- `cargo check -p kovan --all-targets` clean, native and `--target aarch64-linux-android`.
- `cargo test --release -p kovan --lib --tests`: 177 lib + 15 kovan-cli + 17 e2e + 7 digitiser-synthetic, all passing (5 new table_ocr unit tests included).
- `cargo doc -p kovan --no-deps`: no new warnings vs. baseline (fixed one intra-doc link to a private item introduced by this change).
- GUI binary smoke-tested under xvfb-run: reaches the same WGPU-surface-creation failure point as every other GUI smoke test this session (no GPU/DRI in this sandbox) -- an environment limitation, not a code defect. Full interactive verification of the new tab is not possible here and is disclosed as such.

Known limitations (by design, documented in the module doc): no table/column/border detection (whitespace heuristic only), no .traineddata model download (operator supplies the path).

Not committed/pushed yet per this workspace's never-auto-commit rule -- pending the next stop-hook trigger or explicit request.

description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12, and PRE-EXISTING (byte-identical on d9abc55616 and on the TUAS-convention branch, so not introduced by the boundary work).

SETUP. Forward-only advected thermal front, no reversal. L=4 m, A=0.02 m2, 4 MPa water seeded 400 K, inlet junction 450 K, prescribed 3.2 kg/s inlet, fixed 4 MPa outlet pressure, PIMPLE(3,2) at 0.3 under-relaxation, dt=5 ms, 12000 steps.

SYMPTOM. A single-cell enthalpy spike parks at the SECOND-TO-LAST cell (the outlet-adjacent neighbour) and does not decay. Worst overshoot above the inlet junction enthalpy, as a fraction of the 215.4 kJ/kg span between seed and inlet:
  n=8   39.20%  (profile tail ... 748.1, 750.6, 835.3, 750.5)
  n=16  41.36%
  n=32  42.33%  (tail ... 785.7, 777.3, 842.1, 777.1)
  n=64  42.61%  (tail ... 801.3, 787.1, 842.6, 786.9)

KEY POINT: it does NOT converge with mesh refinement - it SATURATES at ~42.6%. A dispersive truncation error would shrink. The spike is always at index n-2 and is a classic odd-even/checkerboard mode anchored at the fixed-pressure outlet.

DISTINCT FROM op-1fyp. op-1fyp records fvc::div(phi,he) as pure central differencing giving 10-15% over/undershoot at an advected front. That is a travelling-front effect and is mesh-convergent. This is boundary-localised, 3-4x larger, and mesh-INVARIANT, so it is a separate defect - most likely the outlet pressure/velocity BC pairing (boundary phi is never pressure-corrected, cf op-nnqi) rather than the interior scheme.

WHY IT MATTERS. For a boiling stream an enthalpy overshoot of this size can push a (p,h) flash out of range and panic. It also sets the floor on any enthalpy-boundedness assertion: the reversal V&V test flow_reversal_keeps_enthalpy_bounded_between_terminals has to carry a forward-only control arm and assert relative to it, because the scheme violates boundedness by ~39% before any reversal is involved.

REPRO: crates/tampines-steam-tables, tests::flow_reversal_keeps_enthalpy_bounded_between_terminals (forward-only control arm).
title: TampinesSteamArray: outlet-anchored odd-even enthalpy oscillation, ~40% of span, NOT mesh-convergent
